artists.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

Split Enz.biography: Split Enz were a New Zealand band of the 1970s and early 1980s featuring Phil Judd and brothers Tim Finn and Neil Finn. They achieved chart success in New Zealand, Australia, and Canada during the early 1980s’ most notably with the single "I Got You", and built a cult following elsewhere. Their musical style was eclectic and original, incorporating influences from art rock, vaudeville, swing, punk, rock, new wave, and pop.

perplexity.description:
Time and Tide," released in April 1982 by Split Enz on A&M Records, is the band's seventh studio album, showcasing a blend of rock and pop with strong new wave influences. The album features a polished, contemporary pop/rock sound that reflects the band's evolution from their earlier art-rock style to a more streamlined and accessible approach. Produced by Hugh Padgham and Split Enz, it was recorded in Sydney and highlights the songwriting talents of Tim and Neil Finn, with tracks characterized by tight arrangements and a balance of energetic rhythms and melodic hooks.

In the context of Split Enz's discography, "Time and Tide" followed the 1981 album "Waiata" and preceded the commercially successful "Conflicting Emotions" (1983). While it did not achieve major international breakthrough in the UK or US, the album was well-received in Australia and New Zealand, going gold within two weeks of release there. Band members have regarded it as one of their best works, with its refined production and strong songwriting marking a high point before internal tensions grew during subsequent projects. The album's style sits firmly within the early 1980s new wave and pop/rock milieu, combining catchy melodies with a polished, radio-friendly sound.
